button.intent: A control that performs an action. If it navigates, it is an anchor and nothing here applies.
button.namespaceNote: Bootstrap keeps `btn-group`, `btn-toolbar` and `btn-close` behind the same prefix while they are container and icon components, so the lookahead marks where this component's authority ends. Everything else under `btn-` is claimed on purpose: an unrecognised variant is what the allowlist exists to catch.

size.intent: Physical size. Orthogonal to emphasis — a secondary button can be small without becoming a different pattern.

medium.intent: The default. Adds no class, so most call sites name no size at all.

small.intent: Dense rows: the order table, inline actions.

large.intent: The single call to action on a marketing page.

primary.intent: The main action on a screen.

secondary.intent: A supporting action beside a primary one.

success.intent: An action that completes or approves something — confirm, publish, mark delivered.

warning.intent: An action that needs a second look before it happens — put on hold, flag for review.

danger.intent: An action that is hard to undo: delete, revoke, cancel an order.

info.intent: An action that reveals more without changing anything — details, help, preview.

primary-outline.intent: Primary emphasis without a fill, for when several actions sit together and one filled button per group is enough.
primary-outline.notes: Outline is a separate PATTERN here, not a modifier, because Bootstrap renames the class (`btn-outline-primary`) rather than adding one. Bulma adds `is-outlined` alongside, so the same visual idea is a modifier there. This is the sort of difference `intent` exists to carry across a library change.

secondary-outline.intent: The quietest bordered action. Cancel, back, dismiss.

danger-outline.intent: A destructive action that should not shout — a delete sitting in a row of other actions.

link.intent: An action styled as text, for tertiary placement inside dense surfaces.

neutral.intent: A button coloured by an absolute palette name rather than a role.
neutral.reason: `light` and `dark` are fixed palette entries, not theme roles. They do not invert, so a light button stays light on a dark theme — this is a measured fact about the library, not a matter of taste, which is why it is the one refusal recorded this early.

card.intent: A bounded surface grouping related content. Anatomy — header, body, footer, images — belongs to Bootstrap; this records only which kinds of card exist.
card.namespaceNote: Only the ROOT class is governed. `card-body`, `card-title` and the rest are the library's anatomy, and a ledger that enumerated them would be redocumenting Bootstrap. The rule across this file: the ledger owns the variant, the library owns the parts.

nav.intent: Navigation surfaces: the top bar and the sidebar. Which links they hold is the application's business.

menu.intent: A vertical menu of destinations, in a sidebar. The primary way this product moves between sections.

tabs.intent: Switching between views of the same thing, without leaving the page.

field.intent: A form control and its label.

select.intent: A choice from a known list.

check.intent: A boolean, or one of a set.

label.intent: The name of a field. Always present — a placeholder is not a label.
